label: prop:interface-band-between-isospin-weights
title: The admissible interface band $[z-h,\,z]$ lies strictly between $\mu_-$ and $\mu_+$
html:
Proposition. The admissible interface band [z-h,\,z] lies strictly between \mu_- and \mu_+

Let \mu = z + d with d \in [-h,\,0] be an admissible interface scalar, so that \mu ranges over the band [z-h,\,z]. Under convention D, whenever the two reduced inequalities

  q - z \;<\; (z-h)\,(q+q^{-1}),
  \qquad
  z\,(q+q^{-1}) \;<\; z + q^{-1}

hold, every admissible \mu satisfies

  \boxed{\;\; \mu_- \;<\; \mu \;<\; \mu_+ . \;\;}

Two separations, both conditional and both checked

The upper separation says the triplet weight lies above the band's ceiling, z < \mu_+. Its reduced form z(q+q^{-1}) < z+q^{-1} is, after substituting z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1), equivalent to q^{5} < q^{2}+1 and therefore holds for q < 1.193859.

The lower separation says the singlet weight lies below the band's floor, \mu_- < z-h. Its reduced form is q - z < (z-h)(q+q^{-1}), which under convention D holds for q < 1.465571.

The substrate parameter clears both, with 7.56\,\% of margin on the tighter of the two. Neither is a knife-edge, and neither can be repaired by a better choice of q: moving q upward past 1.193859 closes the upper separation only by moving \mu_+ into the band, which is not the same as reaching it from inside.

Both hypotheses are carried explicitly rather than folded into the statement, because they are convention-dependent and one of them fails elsewhere. The band lies strictly between the two isospin weights given the reduced inequalities; establishing them is a separate, per-convention obligation.

Convention-dependence, stated rather than buried

Under convention C the lower separation fails. There \mu_- = 0.303675 sits inside the band [0.290260,\, 0.499320], and only the upper separation survives. The strict betweenness is a phenomenon of convention D, and quoting it without the convention would be a misstatement of the same kind the trace-convention registry exists to prevent.

Convention D trades one agreement for another here. It gains the deuteron --- the band now contains B_{\mathrm{AME}}({}^2\mathrm{H}), reached at d = -0.11923\,h, where under convention C the entire band sat 30.69\,\% above it --- and it loses the singlet's reachability. That trade is a fact about the two conventions and is recorded as such, not resolved here.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs --- real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here. At q_0 = 1.10997858275138080759 under convention D:

quantity value at q_0 position
\mu_- (T=0) 0.24729788674803459841 below the floor
z-h (floor) 0.40362773835082593616 63.22\,\% above \mu_-
z (ceiling) 0.61268803714646525160 ---
\mu_+ (T=1) 0.75270211325196540159 22.85\,\% above z

The two misses are 63.22\,\% and 22.85\,\% of the quantity each is measured against. Neither is a margin a refinement absorbs.
